name: Strike Anywhere
label: Jade Tree
lede: Strike Anywhere borrowed its name from a song by singer Thomas Barnett's old band and spent two decades turning Richmond's buried history into tuneful, angry hardcore. A stolen notebook and a Weimar-era antifascist logo got into the story along the way.

eras.title: Named for an Inquisition song
eras.text: When Inquisition ended, singer Thomas Barnett started over in Richmond under the name of one of its songs. Within a year there was an EP and a month on the road with As Friends Rust.

years.h: Thomas Barnett starts Strike Anywhere in Richmond with a borrowed name
years.p: The name comes from a song by his previous band Inquisition. Matt Smith, Matt Sherwood, Garth Petrie and Eric Kane join him, and that lineup holds for eight years.

yt: Full set at the Firehouse, Wayne NJ, November 2000
years.h: Chorus of One EP arrives on Red Leader and No Idea
years.p: It's the band's debut record. Bridge 9 founder Chris Wrenn says he's been a fan since this one.

years.h: Four weeks on the road with As Friends Rust
years.p: The first US tour pairs the band with [[As Friends Rust|2f106f2f-5990-4f50-9590-3fa8da941f98]], the Florida melodic hardcore band, with stops at Mixed Messages in Minneapolis and the Pheer Festival in College Park, Maryland.

eras.title: Jade Tree and a Richmond history lesson
eras.text: Jade Tree signed the band in early 2001, and Brian McTernan produced both of its Jade Tree albums at Salad Days in Maryland. The songs take on police brutality, globalization and Richmond's secret past, and they're built for singing along.

years.h: Jade Tree signs Strike Anywhere
years.p: The Wilmington, Delaware label picks up the band two months before it records its debut. A 7-inch for Fat Wreck's Fat Club series follows that year.

years.h: [[Brian McTernan|eda2cb2f-b2c6-4e74-9fd7-49ea52df4172]] records the debut at his own Salad Days studio
years.p: He produces, engineers and mixes Change Is a Sound in Baltimore, and will make the next three records too.

years.h: Change Is a Sound is a debut built on local stories
years.p: 'Sunset on 32nd' takes on police brutality and 'Chalkline' women's rights. The cover photo, shot on the band's first European tour, has Tony Pence of the punk band Deep Sleep at its edge.
years.xp:
Barnett described the record as "built on a lot of local experiences, like local stories." The liner notes backed vegetarianism, the living wage movement and the fight against corporate globalization.

Asked about turning down a Soul Brains supporting slot, he said the band "had been out for like 9 weeks already and we had to get home and get back to work." Metal Hammer gave the album 5/10.

years.h: Genoa Benefit EP comes out on Scene Police
years.p: It's tied to the summer's protests against the G8 summit in Genoa.

yt: Live at Camden Underworld, London, November 16, 2001
years.h: Strike Anywhere plays the Camden Underworld while a camera rolls
years.p: London, November 16, three weeks into a European tour with As Friends Rust. Punkervision turns the footage into a DVD in December 2002.
years.xp:
The tour ran from October 29 to December 5, 2001. The London set came out as Live at Camden Underworld, a split video with As Friends Rust.

The band has always let fans tape its shows for personal, non-commercial use, and works with the Internet Archive to host those recordings.

years.h: A live 'Sunset on 32nd' joins the Amadou Diallo memorial compilation
years.p: 1157 Wheeler Avenue honors Diallo, whom New York police killed in 1999. The band's police-brutality song is on it.

years.h: Someone steals Thomas Barnett's lyric notebooks from his car
years.p: Weeks before the band records Exit English, the notebooks of lyrics and song ideas are gone, so the rest of the band writes too.
years.xp: Producer [[Brian McTernan|eda2cb2f-b2c6-4e74-9fd7-49ea52df4172]] then put Barnett through eight hours a day of vocals at Salad Days, until McTernan was satisfied. Barnett remembered him as really hard on the band.

years.big: "Thinking for yourself and not embracing American ideals worldwide"
yt: Full set at CBGB, New York, 2003
years.h: Exit English goes digging in Richmond's past
years.p: That's guitarist Matt Smith on the title. Barnett later adds that it also alludes to English colonialism, and the songs cover slave insurrections, women's riots and the Confederate army burning the city.
years.xp:
AllMusic's Charles Spano called it "as fun as it is serious." The album also has more melodic harmony guitar than the debut.

'Blaze' has Barnett quoting Percy Bysshe Shelley's The Masque of Anarchy. 'Fifth Estate' is a hardcore power ballad about mass media control, and 'In the Fingernails' is an anti-war song that opens with handclaps and tambourine.

years.h: 'Refusal' goes in a skateboard game, 'Chalk Line' goes acoustic
years.p: 'Refusal' is on the 2003 Tony Hawk's Underground soundtrack. An acoustic 'Chalk Line' is on Fearless Records' Punk Goes Acoustic.

years.h: To Live in Discontent is a live farewell to Jade Tree
years.p: Jade Tree co-releases it with Chunksaah, the Bouncing Souls' label.

years.h: Strike Anywhere spends the summer on the 2005 Vans Warped Tour
years.p: Wake Up Screaming, the documentary about that tour, features the band. 'Question the Answer' also lands on Tony Hawk's American Wasteland.

eras.title: A new guitarist and an old logo
eras.text: Strike Anywhere moved to Fat Wreck Chords, then Bridge 9, still recording with McTernan. Founding guitarist Matt Sherwood left after a show in New Zealand, and the fourth album took its name from the antifascist symbol on the band's logo.

years.cap: Strike Anywhere at ABC ProHc 10, Sao Bernardo do Campo, Brazil
years.h: Weekend sessions add up to Dead FM on Fat Wreck
years.p: The band records over nine months of weekends between tours. Opener 'Sedition' draws on Thomas Barnett's grandfather's work on the Manhattan Project.
years.xp:
The album is 15 songs in just over 31 minutes. Punknews.org ranked it No. 4 on its list of the 20 best releases of 2006.

Barnett said the politics had shifted from events toward more sociological ideas about why these things happen.

years.cap: Strike Anywhere at a festival in Taipei, February 28, 2007
years.h: Auckland is where founding guitarist Matt Sherwood plays his last show
years.p: Mark Miller steps in, and Thomas Barnett, Matt Smith, Garth Petrie and Eric Kane carry on.

years.cap: Thomas Barnett at the Harvest of Hope festival, St. Augustine, Florida, March 2009
years.h: Chris Wrenn's Bridge 9 gets Strike Anywhere
years.p: Wrenn, the label's founder, has been a fan since the debut EP. The band is in the studio for its first Bridge 9 record by that May and June.
years.xp:
Wrenn described the label as a "cool combination of hardcore roots and culture, a love for the life and message."

Strike Anywhere recorded Iron Front at Salad Days in May and June 2009 with McTernan.

years.h: After years on the logo, the Three Arrows get an album
years.p: The band's logo had long echoed the Three Arrows of the Iron Front, a German antifascist group from the Weimar Republic's last years. The fourth album takes the name.
years.xp:
Two singles came first: 'Hand of Glory' on July 3 and 'I'm Your Opposite Number' on September 21. The album has 13 songs in 31 minutes.

Justin Staggs directed the video for 'I'm Your Opposite Number', filmed in Minneapolis and released in early 2010.

years.cap: Sala Apolo, Barcelona, 2010, on the tour with Pennywise
years.h: The Iron Front tour runs through 2010 with Propagandhi and Pennywise
years.p: Dates cross North America, Europe, Australia and New Zealand, with Crime in Stereo and Four Year Strong on some bills.
years.xp: Festival stops included The Fest, Groezrock, and Reading and Leeds.

eras.title: A decade of live records
eras.text: Two live albums, a promised new one and a long wait. In 2020 Strike Anywhere came back with seven new songs.

years.h: Bridge 9 puts out an acoustic record and a plugged-in one
years.p: In Defiance of Empty Times reworks songs acoustically, and Live at the Montage Music Hall catches the band plugged in.

years.h: Barnett tells an interviewer a fifth album is coming
years.p: In December 2016 he says he's writing it. What arrives in 2020 is a seven-song EP.

yt: hate5six full set, Croydon PA, March 17, 2019
years.h: Eleven years later, Nightmares of the West
years.p: Seven songs on Pure Noise Records, built from ideas the bandmates traded over the 2010s. It's the first new material since Iron Front.
